conceptBreakdown.content:
The classification of elements organizes chemical diversity into a systematic framework defined by electronic architecture:

1. **Dobereiner's Triads (1829)**: Elements arranged in groups of three with similar properties. The atomic mass of the middle element is approximately the arithmetic mean of the other two (e.g., $\text{Li} (7) + \text{K} (39) / 2 = 23 = \text{Na}$). Failed for heavier and transition elements.
2. **Newlands' Law of Octaves (1865)**: Arranging elements by atomic mass revealed every eighth element resembled the first (like musical notes). Applicable strictly up to Calcium ($Z=20$).
3. **Lothar Meyer's Curves (1869)**: Plotted atomic volume against atomic mass. Strongly electropositive alkali metals occupied curve peaks, alkaline earths occupied descending slopes, and halogens occupied ascending slopes.
4. **Mendeleev's Periodic Table (1869)**: Formulated the classical Periodic Law: *The physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their Atomic Masses*. Successfully predicted undiscovered elements (**Eka-Aluminium $\rightarrow$ Gallium**, **Eka-Silicon $\rightarrow$ Germanium**, **Eka-Boron $\rightarrow$ Scandium**). Suffered from anomalous pairs ($\text{Ar}$ before $\text{K}$, $\text{Te}$ before $\text{I}$) and lacked positions for isotopes.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.2 Moseley’s Experiment & The Modern Periodic Law (1913)
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.2 Moseley’s Experiment & The Modern Periodic Law (1913)
conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
MOSELEY'S X-RAY FREQUENCY LAW
                       
   Graph of √ν vs Atomic Mass (A) ──────► NON-LINEAR CURVE
   Graph of √ν vs Atomic Number (Z) ────► PERFECT STRAIGHT LINE

   √ν = a(Z - b)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Henry Moseley bombarded various metallic targets with high-energy cathode rays and measured the characteristic $K_\alpha$ X-ray emission frequencies:

$$\mathbf{\sqrt{\nu} = a(Z - b)}$$

where $\nu$ is the frequency of emitted X-rays, $Z$ is the atomic number, $a$ is a proportionality constant, and $b$ is the screening constant ($b \approx 1$ for $K_\alpha$ lines).

• **Modern Periodic Law**: *The physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their Atomic Numbers ($Z$)*, reflecting the underlying subshell electronic configurations.

conceptBreakdown.heading: 1.3 IUPAC Nomenclature for Superheavy Elements (Z > 100)
conceptBreakdown.title: 1.3 IUPAC Nomenclature for Superheavy Elements (Z > 100)
conceptBreakdown.content:
Superheavy elements ($Z > 100$) receive systematic temporary names derived directly from their atomic number digits with suffix **-ium**:

• **Numerical Roots**: $0 = \text{nil (n)}$, $1 = \text{un (u)}$, $2 = \text{bi (b)}$, $3 = \text{tri (t)}$, $4 = \text{quad (q)}$, $5 = \text{pent (p)}$, $6 = \text{hex (h)}$, $7 = \text{sept (s)}$, $8 = \text{oct (o)}$, $9 = \text{enn (e)}$.
• **Phonetic Rules**: $\text{enn} + \text{nil} = \text{ennil}$; $\text{bi} + \text{ium} = \text{bium}$; $\text{tri} + \text{ium} = \text{trium}$.

• **Examples**:
- $Z = 104 \implies \text{un} + \text{nil} + \text{quad} + \text{ium} = \mathbf{\text{Unnilquadium (Unq)}}$ (Official: Rutherfordium, $\text{Rf}$).
- $Z = 118 \implies \text{un} + \text{un} + \text{oct} + \text{ium} = \mathbf{\text{Ununoctium (Uuo)}}$ (Official: Oganesson, $\text{Og}$).
- $Z = 119 \implies \text{un} + \text{un} + \text{enn} + \text{ium} = \mathbf{\text{Ununennium (Uue)}}$.

quickRevision: Moseley's law: √ν = a(Z - b) proves Z is the fundamental atomic variable.
Modern Periodic Law: Properties are periodic functions of Atomic Number Z.
IUPAC superheavy naming uses roots: nil(0), un(1), bi(2), tri(3), quad(4), pent(5), hex(6), sept(7), oct(8), enn(9) + ium.
keyFormulae: IUPAC Name = Root₁ + Root₂ + Root₃ + ium
